message.reasoning_content:
We need to read the facts and determine which crimes are directly supported.

Facts: Two defendants, Wang and Gu, got into a quarrel with Liu, beat each other. Liu later died due to acute coronary attack triggered by the fight, with causal link. Also Liu had bilateral nasal bone fractures, assessed as light injury level 2. So they caused bodily injury (light injury) and death. The prosecution says they are charged with intentional injury causing death (故意伤害致人死亡). In Chinese criminal law, that is "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury) with result of death, which can be punished as "故意伤害致人死亡" (i.e., a specific form). Also possibly "过失致人死亡"? But they acted intentionally to injure, not to kill. So the appropriate charge is "故意伤害罪". Also possibly "故意伤害致人死亡" is a specific crime, but the name is still "故意伤害罪". Could there be "故意伤害致人死亡" as a separate charge? Usually the charge is "故意伤害罪" with the circumstance of death, but sometimes they list "故意伤害致人死亡". The question: "用法定罪名". The law has "故意伤害罪" (Article 234). If death results, the penalty is higher. So the charge is "故意伤害罪". Also could be "故意伤害致人死亡" is not a separate statutory name. So only one crime.

Thus answer: [罪名]故意伤害罪<eoa>

Check if any other crimes: maybe "聚众斗殴"? But they were just two people. Not "聚众斗殴". Also "非法拘禁"? No. So only intentional injury.

Thus final.
